summary: Configured daily logrotate for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 (rotate 7, compress, copytruncate) via /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app, verified the rotation preserves writer continuity, then restarted node1 and confirmed the config, timer, and rotation behavior all survived the reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: found /var/log/inventory/app.log, active logrotate.timer (systemd, daily), no existing logrotate.d entry for the app
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with: daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Ran logrotate dry-run to validate config syntax
Seeded app.log content and launched a background writer appending lines every second
Forced rotation (logrotate -f) while the writer was actively appending
Verified app.log continued receiving new writer lines uninterrupted after rotation, and prior content was compressed into app.log.1.gz
Confirmed logrotate.timer is enabled and active (systemd OnCalendar=daily)
Captured baseline boot_id, uptime, log state, and logrotate/timer health before restart
Issued a backgrounded sudo systemctl reboot so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Confirmed boot_id changed (06339ff3-... -> ac51707f-...) and uptime reset, proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart: verified /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app persisted, logrotate.timer active/enabled, prior app.log and app.log.1.gz still present
Post-restart functional re-test: appended a line, forced another rotation, appended again, confirmed app.log.1.gz/app.log.2.gz rotation chain and continued writability

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation with 7 kept compressed rotations configured for /var/log/inventory/app.log
evidence.summary: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily/rotate 7/compress; logrotate -d dry-run and -v verbose run confirm 'after 1 days ... (7 rotations)' pattern is parsed correctly, and logrotate.timer (OnCalendar=daily) is active/enabled

evidence.requirement: Application can continue writing after rotation (copytruncate)
evidence.summary: A background writer appending to app.log every second was left running through a forced rotation; post-rotation app.log contained the writer's later lines ('writer line 3/4/5') with no interruption or errors, while earlier content was moved into app.log.1.gz
Captured boot_id 06339ff3-9f53-4e1d-9bf4-1210144ee001, uptime, healthy logrotate dry-run output, rotated files present, and logrotate.timer active/enabled

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 1; systemctl reboot' returned 'reboot command dispatched' immediately, then subsequent calls failed with connection reset/timeout confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: Polled node1 through disconnect until reconnection; boot_id changed from 06339ff3-9f53-4e1d-9bf4-1210144ee001 to ac51707f-685f-4fcc-93aa-fc0c33e1b032 with a fresh uptime -s timestamp, proving an actual reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of logrotate config and functional rotation
evidence.summary: After restart, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app persisted unchanged, logrotate.timer remained active/enabled, prior app.log/app.log.1.gz were intact, and a fresh append+forced-rotation+append cycle produced app.log.1.gz/app.log.2.gz with app.log immediately writable again
